narrative.text:
NARRATIVE:

ENTRY:

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] (A# [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] ) claims to have last entered the United States illegally by crossing the Rio Grande River near Hildalgo, Texas in July of 2014. During a later interview, he stated that he entered the United States through the Hidalgo port of entry with a border crossing card. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] has no proof that this is when he actually entered the United States, and there is no record stating that this was in fact his last entry date.

TRAVEL:

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claimed to have left his home in San Pedro Sula, Copan, Honduras because he planned to travel to Michigan to reside and work. He claimed that he crossed into both Guatemala and Mexico illegally. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he traveled through Guatemala and Mexico by bus until he reached Reynosa, Tamaulipas, Mexico. Once there, he hired a smuggler to lead him across the United States/Mexico Border. He claimed that he agreed to pay $7000 to the smuggler to lead him across the border. He claims that the smuggler led him and another man illegally into the United States by crossing the Rio Grande River in the July of 2014. He said that after he crossed they walked for one day to a house in McAllen, Texas. He stayed at that house for three (3) days and then traveled by car to Michigan. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] said that during his travel, he never passed through any immigration checkpoints. None of [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] travel claims could be verified. None of [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] entry/travel information could be verified.

INADMISSIBILITY:

Subject is a native and citizen of Honduras as are both of his parents. He has never had any documents that would allow him to be or remain in the United States legally. Subject is inadmissible under Section 212(a)(6)(A)(I) of the INA, in that he entered the United States at a time or place not designated by the Attorney General and was not then admitted or paroled after inspection by an immigration officer.

FACTS OF ARREST:

At approximately 8:00 am on May 23, 2017, Border Patrol Agent (BPA) [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was dispatched by Supervisory Border Patrol Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] to assist the Michigan State Police (MSP) with identifying three subjects, who had no United States government or state issued identification, on [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] near Fenton, MI. When stopped by MSP, the three (3) subjects presented the Trooper with Foreign National Identification Cards. BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] arrived at approximately 9:00 am and identified himself as a United States Border Patrol Agent to the five subjects. Trooper [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] had pulled over the vehicle for speeding. While assisting Trooper [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] in identifying the subjects, BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] determined that three of the subjects were not in possession any valid immigration documents that would allow them to be, or remain in the United States legally. All three subjects freely admitted to being citizens and nationals of Honduras, Guatemala, and Mexico and to have illegally entered the United States, and had no documentation to allow them to remain or be in the United States. They were positively identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] then took these three subjects into custody. The driver and front seat passenger were both found to be citizens of Mexico, legally present in the United States. Trooper [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] cited the driver for speeding and released him from the scene with the vehicle. At approximately 9:20 am BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] arrived on scene to assist with transporting the three subjects back to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Station. Record checks were ran on [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , through [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Dispatch, and [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] fingerprinting revealed the following criminal and immigration history:

IMMIGRATION HISTORY:

NONE FOUND

CRIMINAL HISTORY:

NONE FOUND

EMPLOYMENT:

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] works for [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] . He claims that he is paid $12.00 an hour

CONSULAR RIGHTS:

Subject was provided his I-826 rights and advised of his right to speak with the Honduran Consulate, which he declined. Subject was also provided with a list of pro bono legal service providers. Subject was offered a Stipulated Removal, which he declined.

HEALTH:

Subject claims to be, and appears to be, in good health. DISPOSITION: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was processed as a WA/NTA. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] his property and money are being transported to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Police Department.
